content:
Miss your course's English requirement by half a band and most admission systems in the world send you home to retake a test. The UK, mostly, does not. Pre-sessional English courses are university-run programmes that start in spring or summer, train you up to the level your degree requires, and end in an internal assessment that — passed — upgrades your conditional offer to unconditional. For applicants sitting at IELTS 5.5 or 6.0 against a 6.5 requirement, it is often the difference between losing a year and starting on time.

How long, and what it costs

Course length is set by the gap between your current score and the requirement: roughly 4 to 6 weeks for a 0.5-band gap, 10 to 12 weeks for a full band, and up to 20 or even 30 weeks for bigger deficits. Universities price by the week or by the block, and published 2026 fees give you the honest range. Sheffield charges £525 per week for its year-round pre-sessional. Middlesex runs 6 to 30 weeks from £2,700 to £11,100. Sussex's 10-week on-campus course is £4,270 and its 16-week course £6,881, with fees frozen from the previous year. Westminster's 13-week course is £5,560. Across the sector, £3,000 to £3,600 buys a 6-week course and £8,000 to £10,000 a full 20-week one, with accommodation on top.

The visa wrinkle: a second CAS

Here is the part that catches people out. Unless your university issues a combined CAS, the pre-sessional course gets its own Student visa, its own financial evidence and its own arrival date — you fly in for the English course, pass it, and only then receive the CAS for your degree and apply again if a combined route was not used. Many universities now run combined CAS arrangements that wrap both stages into one visa, but policies differ and the documentary requirements differ with them, so ask the question at offer stage rather than at booking stage. Our step-by-step UK student visa guide covers the financial evidence rules that apply to whichever route you take.

Pass requirements: not a formality

Pre-sessional assessment is internal but real. You will be tested on academic writing, reading, listening and seminar skills through coursework and a final assessment, and while the overwhelming majority pass — universities design these courses to graduate their own offer-holders — a small number fail or are given reduced conditions each year. Attendance rules are enforced through visa compliance: miss sessions and you can be reported, which jeopardises both the English outcome and your immigration status. Treat the course as the first term of your degree, not as a holiday with homework.

Pre-sessional versus retaking IELTS

Run the numbers honestly. One more IELTS attempt costs £180 to £220 and six weeks of waiting, and if you are confident of the extra half band it is obviously cheaper. But IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted everywhere, test dates fill up in peak season, and a second miss costs another month. The pre-sessional also buys things a test cannot: academic writing conventions, referencing, seminar participation and a settled visa status before your cohort arrives. For research-bound applicants, remember that doctoral English rules are set department by department — our UK PhD English requirements comparison explains where pre-sessional routes exist at PhD level too. And if you are weighing the test-free MOI route instead, start with our UK without IELTS guide before you book either option.

Booking timeline for September starters

Pre-sessional courses run on unforgiving calendars. A 20-week course starts in April, 16-week courses in late April or May, 10-week courses in June, and 6-week courses in July or August, all finishing just before term. Work backwards from your degree's start date: you need the IELTS result that triggers the conditional offer, the CAS and the separate visa (unless combined) before the course begins, and visa processing in peak summer adds weeks. Applicants who discover in May that they need a 10-week course frequently cannot get a visa appointment in time — the course was available, the calendar was not.

Money-wise, ask two questions before booking. Does your university offer a combined CAS that lets one visa cover both stages, saving a second application fee and health surcharge? And is accommodation guaranteed for pre-sessional students — many universities reserve halls for exactly this group, which removes the hardest part of an early arrival. Pass the course and your unconditional status lands before the main intake; our UK accommodation guide covers the housing choices that follow.

Studentships with January deadlines to aim at

Finish your pre-sessional in September and these January-close competitions become a realistic target rather than a fantasy. Each card below is live in our database with verified dates.

  • ESRC White Rose DTP Studentships 2027/28 at the University of Leeds — January-closing social science studentships at Leeds. Deadline: 17:00 (UK Time) 20 January 2027.
  • UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Awards at University College London 2027 — UCL's main engineering and physical sciences round
  • Fully Funded PhD in Psychology at University of East Anglia 2027 — a fully funded January psychology PhD. Deadline: 14 January 2027.
  • International PhD Studentships at University of Reading 2027 — Reading's central studentship competition. Deadline: 15 January 2027.
  • Future Fluid Dynamics CDT PhD, University of Leeds 2027 — fluid dynamics CDT projects at Leeds. Deadline: 7 January 2027.
  • Computing Science PhD Studentships, University of Glasgow 2027 — Glasgow computing science studentships. Deadline: 31 January 2027.
